QF.id: VIII Sales Practices and Investor Protection Services_4

question.text: The best execution obligation of a broker means:

answer.text: The broker must take all reasonable steps to obtain the best possible result for the client considering price, cost, speed, and likelihood of execution
The broker must guarantee the best price in the entire market
The broker must execute orders only at the opening price
The broker can execute at any price that benefits their proprietary book

explanation.text: The Logic: The best-execution obligation is the duty on a broker to take all reasonable steps to obtain the best possible result for the client when handling and executing orders. The standard considers multiple execution factors together - price, total cost (including charges), speed of execution, and the likelihood of execution and settlement - rather than only the best displayed price at a single instant. The obligation is one of reasonable diligence, not a guaranteed outcome. The Trap: Best execution does not promise the absolute best price across the entire market, does not lock execution to the opening price, and does not allow a broker to execute at prices that benefit the broker's proprietary book over the client. Note: The "price, cost, speed and likelihood of execution" phrasing is not stated in the cited pages of the NISM-Series-VIII Equity Derivatives workbook, which on the pages checked covers timely order execution, suitable advice/fair sales conduct, and complaint categories for order-execution errors. The framing above is general broker-conduct / best-execution regulatory knowledge.
